One day in September 2009, I received a query as under : 


“Sir, I got my daughter married on the 14 Sept, 2009. My son-in-law who is employed in 
Germany has already got confirmed return flight ticket for 30 of October. My effort to get 
visa for my daughter has not met with success to this date( 20/10/2009). Will she be able 
to accompany her husband ? ”, questioned a worried father and gave a horary number ‘24’ 
for analysis. 


Analysis was done : at Palghat,10*49’ N / 76* 39° E 
:on 21st October, 2009 ; Wednesday ; at 10 hr.30 minutes. 
Horary number >“ 24“ K.P. Ayanamsa : 23* 53’ 42 “ 


Analysis :- 


First of all let us check whether the desire of the father will get fulfilled or not . This can be 
known from the 11 house. Here, in this horary chart, the sub lord of the 11th cusp is 
Saturn, who is the lord of 11 as well,-indicating that he will have his wish granted since 
Saturn is in direct motion. 


Having found that the father’s desire will get fulfilled, we will analyse and cross-check the 
fate in store for his daughter. 


We have to look at the cuspal sub lord of 12‘* bhaava of the horary chart erected to see 
whether the daughter will go abroad. 


The cuspal sub lord of the 12th house is Jupiter, lord of 9,12, in direct motion and in the 
star and sub of Mars in 3. Thus Jupiter signifies 3 (leaving her present place of residence), 
9 (long journey) and 12 (new environment of foreign land), thereby confirming that she will 
join her husband in his travel back to Germany. 


When will this be? 


The joint dasa operation of the significators of houses 3/9/12 taken together will indicate 
her departure. 


As per horary chart, the dasa of Saturn is on. Saturn is in the sub of Mercury lord of 3. No 
planet is in the stars of Mercury and Mercury is the CSL of 3-9 having no planet in its 
stars. Bhukti period is that of Sun, who is in the star of Mars lord of 3. Antra lord Mars 
ends on 25-10-2009 thus I select next Rahu antra from 25-10-2009 to 16-12-2009. Rahu 
is occupant of 9, conjoined with Jupiter lord of 9, 12. Hence Saturn dasa, Sun bhukti and 
Rahu antra (25-10-2009 to 16-12-2009) is potent to cause the event happen. 


So, I informed the father that she will be able to travel abroad on the 30 October along 
with her husband.

\HRHEEEEE & 
In recent years we have witnessed a sudden boom in real estate activity — purchase and 
sale of buildings and flats. In this article, I propose to discuss the question of sale of 
house property about which astrologers are very often approached for prediction. 











It is well known that in astrology, the fourth house, apart from other significations also 
indicates all types of immovable property such as land /house/flat/and buildings. 


The seventh house in a horoscope speaks about the person with whom we deal or 
transact. When a person desires to sell a house, the 7 house refers to the purchaser. 


The third house in a horoscope is 12 to 4th—which means the seller losing or parting 
with his house property-whether it is a house or flat or building. 


The fifth house is 11 to 7» (the purchaser) and it tells us about the fulfillment of the wish 
of the buyer and also his gain. 


The tenth house being the 4 from 7 is regarding the house of the purchaser. 

It can be readily seen that 5th and 10 house of the native (seller) will be the 4th and 11t 
of the opposite party, in this case the purchaser and 3 being the 12 to 4 signifies the 
disposal of the property by sale. 


In K.P. astrology, the rules for sale of house property are simple and clear cut. If the 
sub-lord of the 10% signifies 3/5/10, the native will definitely sell his property. This event 
will take place during the DBA period of the significators of these relevant houses. 


If by chance the 11 house is also signified in the combination of planets for sale of 
property, then there is no doubt that the sale will be for a profit. On the other hand, if the 
DBA lords signify 6/8/12—the sale is bound to result in a loss only. 


Against this background let us take a sample chart to study the applicability of these rules 
and principles. The horoscope of a person well-known to me is appended herewith. 

In the horoscope, the tenth cusp sublord is Saturn. Saturn is in 8 and it is the lord of 7 
and 8.. Sublord of Saturn is Mercury in Ascendant, lord of 3 and 12. Saturn also aspects 
the fifth house. 


In view of the significations of 3/5 /10 of the 10 cuspal sublord, it is clear that the sale 
of his property will take place. 


For timing of the event of sale we have to extract the significators of the houses.

dasa and sub dasa lords along with the transit and aspects.

Three Pillars of KP Astrology 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 





(Hil 





Three Pillars 

1. The Hindu zodiac, Placidus house system and Vimshottari dasa system are three pillars 
of KP astrology since they are essential for functioning of KP. The ruling planets are not a 
pillar because KP can be applied without using them. 


Hindu Zodiac 

2. This is the foundation of a KP chart and the basis in application of sign to sign Hindu 
aspects which are practically used in KP. The nature of signs like dual, fruitful or fruitful 
signs is also considered although not so importance is not given to signs like in Vedic 
astrology. 


Placidus Houses System 

3. Theoretical and mathematical criticism is important, but experiment gets the last word. 
The proof is in the practice that has stood the test of time. The Placidus house system 
is commonly used and popular - because it actually works quite well in astrological 
practice. Interpretations of horoscopes bear out. Computation is quick and easy for 
astrologers who are not highly trained in mathematics. 


4. The Placidus house system, invented by the 17th Century Italian monk Placido de 
Titus, gained popularity in the 19th century due to easy availability via the well-circulated 
and popular Raphael's Ephemeris since 1821. Raphael's ephemeris and houses had ruled 
the astrological world while Prof. K.S. Krishnamurti was doing research and writing KP. 
The most popular Placidus house system, the first to be published as Raphael's Tables of 
Houses (104 pages), is used in calculation of the house -—bhava- based KP chart. The 
Placidus cusps are the basis for consideration of significators by occupation and owner of 
planets. 





5. However nowadays the NASA based accurate Swiss ephemeris is ruling the astrological 
softwares, and so the Raphael's Ephemeris and Tables of Houses are just history. 


6. Despite of the shortcomings in application for the higher Polar latitudes, as England's 
foremost Astrologer Ronald Davison has said, you can play many good tunes on a piano 


KP Ezine May 2015 124 


whose top is defective; hence Placidus system is satisfactory. 


7. The Placidus house system has been used by well known American astrologers like Noel 
Tyl, Liz Greene in their numerous published books. According to "Recent Advances in Natal 
Astrology", compiled by Geoffrey Dean, p 168, in the USA about 80% of individuals who 
seek help from astrologers and 90% of individuals who refer to online horoscopes prefer the 
system of Placidus. 


8. If one has a client out of about one million people living at polar latitudes, the 
Topocentric house system, which has cusps remarkably close to those of Placidus, can be 
used. 


Vimshottari Dasa System 


9. Sage Maharishi Parashara clearly and precisely said in his Brihat Parashara Hora 
Shastra, Vol. II, trans. R. Santhanam, Ranjan Publications, 1984, Ch 46 v12-15, p 507: 


“ Vimsottari Dasa 

12-14. Beginning from Krittika the lords of Dasas (periods) are the Sun, the Moon, Mars, 
Rahu, Jupiter. Saturn, Mercury, Ketu and Venus in that order. Thus if the nakshatras from 
Krittika to the Janma nakshatra (natal constellation) are divided by nine, the remainder will 
signify the lord of the commencing Dasa. The remaining Dasas will be of the planets in the 
order given above. 

In Kaliyuga the natural life span of a human being is generally taken as 120 years. 
Therefore, Vimsottari Dasa is consideredto be the most appropriate and the best of all Dasas. 
15. The periods of Dasas of the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Ralru, Jupiter, Saturn, Merury. Ketu 
and Venus are 6, 10, 7, 18, 16, 19, 17, 7 and 20 in that order.” 


10. Without knowing the rationale of sequence of planet Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu etc. and 
allotted years to planets, 6to Sun, 10 to Moon, 7 to Mars, 18 to Rahu etc. , the Vimshottari 
dasa is the most commonly used dasa for timing of events as foreseen by Sage Parashara 
because it is time tested really working dasa. 


11. The Vimshottari dasa system is used in KP for division of subs according to the 
proportion of years allotted to planets. In fixing the timing of events, the 365 days/ year 
Vimshottari dasa starting from Moon is used. 


12. The 365 days/year Vimshottari dasa starting from Moon has been used by all well 
known astrologers, All well known astrologers like B V Raman, K.S. Krishnamurti, P. S. 
Ssastri, J.N. Basin, Bepin Behari, K N Rao, Sajay Rath, V. K. Choudhry, Dr. K.S. Charak, 
P.V.R. Rayudu. 


13. By taking a month of 30 days and a year of 360 days, one cannot go by the universally 
used Gregorian calendar. Mpreover, if the 360 day year rather than the 365 day year is 
used for the mahadasa calculation, the gap between them would become more and more 
divergent with the dasa period, i.e. 6.25 days (865.25-360) after 1 year, 31.5 days (6.25x6) 
after 5 years, about 6 months after 35 years, a whole year after 70 years, and a native may 
have to celebrate his 72 birthday even while he has yet to complete his 71st year under 
Vimshottari dasa of the 365 day/year. 


14. Regarding the KP ayanmasa, the new KP ayanamsa is preferable. The value of different 
ayanamsa cannot significantly change the dasa balance at birth i.e. for 1 minute difference 


2.70 days for Sun, 4.50 days for Moon, 3.15 days for Mars, 8.10 days for Rahu etc. only. 


15. The total 120 years of Vimshotarri dasa is the natural life span of a human being as 
clearly said by Sage Prashara. So it may not be appropriate to apply the 120 year 


KP Ezine May 2015 125 


Vimshottari dasa for the nation charts whose life span can be more than one circle of 120 
years like USA. 


16. In the case of event charts like oath taking charts of presidents, prime ministers, chief 
ministers for 4 or 5 year term, launching space mission for a particular period, annual 
chart or Hindu new year chart for one year, the application of relevant 4 or 5 year, 
particular period or one year compressed Vimshottari dasa is more appropriate.

Selec on of significators in the birth chart 


By: G.H.W.Silva

In the delineation of a birth chart, we need to select the significators for the particular 
bhava we are interested in. 

According to Krishnamurthi Padhdhathi, the steller method propounded by our late 
Guruji, the significatros for a bhava in the birth chart is selected as follows; 











1) Lord of the bhava, 

2) The planets deposited in the constellations of the lord of the bhava, 
3) The planets occupying the bhava, 

4) The planets deposited in the constellations of the occupiers, and 

5) The planets who are in aspects with the above planets. 


The following birth chart has been analysed to find the period of marriage of the native. In 
analyzing a birth chart on a special matter, we need to find that the native is destined to 
enjoy that result. As for marriage, it is to see whether the native is destined to get married. 
If the answer is yes only, we could proceed further. If the native is denied of marriage, 
there is no point in finding the period of the event. 


This nirayana bhava chart is prepared using Placidus house divisions and planetary 
positions using KP ayanamsa (new), as advised by our Guruji. 


The Ascendant at the time of birth is Sagittarius 16.31.48 and the 1st bhava is extending 
up to Capricorn 16.16.09. The planet Moon is in Sagittarius 19.51.17 and thus, it is in the 
1st bhava. 


The 2d bhava is commencing from Capricorn 16.16.09 and extending up to Aquarius 
18.21.40 enclosing the 24 bhava. The planet Saturn is in Aquarius 17.23.26 in retrograde 
motion. He belongs to the 2" bhava. 


The 34 bhava is from Aquarius 18.21.40 to Pisces 21.11.57 and no planets are deposited 
in this bhava. 


The 4th bhava is from Pisces 21.11.57 to Aries 21.54.11 and no planets are deposited in 
this 4 bhava also. 


From Aries 21.54.11 to Taurus 19.45.56 is the 5 bhava and Rahu is deposited in Taurus 
12.40.54 and belongs to 5 bhava. 


From Taurus 19.45.56 to Gemini 16.31.48 is the 6 bhava and Jupiter is in Gemini 
07.05.40 and belongs to 6 bhava. 


From Gemini 16.31.48 to Cancer 16.16.09 is 74 bhava, from Cancer 16.16.09 to Leo 
18.21.39 is the 8 bhava and from Leo 18.21.39 to Virgo 21.11.57 is the 9% bhava 


respectively. No planets are deposited in these bhavas. 


From Virgo 21.11.57 to Libra 21.54.11 is the 10% bhava. Sun is deposited in Libra 
13.16.29 and thus occupying the 10 bhava.

marriage) is a significator for 7 bhava or 274 bhava (increase of family members) or the 11th 
bhava (fulfillment of expectation), the native is fortunate to get married.

dasha and sub dashas and the transit of the significators during the time of marriage.

lord of the 7 cusp is Venus. This Venus is deposited in a star of Mercury. The sub lord of 
the 76 cusp Venus is the owner of 6 and 11 bhavas and occupying the 12th bhava. 
Mercury is the owner of 7 and 10 bhavas and deposited in the 11 bhava. Accordingly 
this native is destined to get married.

In March 2012, a gentleman from my area visited me and asked to go through his 
horoscope to check weather he is eligible to start a printing shop as his career. In our 
friendly discussion, he disclosed that he had been employed as manager in a printing 
business. But he resigned from the same to start his own printing press as he was unable 
to maintain his family with lower remuneration there. So I proceed with natal chart 
analysis as below. 


Mr. Mahinda, Male, 14th Sept. 1968, 12.25 pm, Kurunegala, North Western Province, Sri 
Lanka, Lat. 07.28.00 N, Long. 80.21.00 E, Asc. Sagittarius, 01° 19' 22", Moon Vimshottari 
Maha Dasa Balance OOY 11M 30D, KP New Ayanamsa 23° 19' 48", Calculated by KPAstro 
4.1 


KP rule to have own press: 

"Press is indicated by Mars, Mercury and Jupiter. Therefore if the sub Lord of the meridian 
is deposited in the constellation of a planet, which is the significator of at least one of the 
three houses 2, 6 & 10 and also if it is connected with Mars and Mercury, one will have 
one’s own press.” 

- KP 6th Reader, page 306, June 2007 Edition. 


My first attempt was to check the chart for promise to have his own press as per the above 
rule. 


The cuspal sub lord (CSL) of 10th and 6th houses Saturn is in the star of Kethu and sub 
of Venus. Saturn is lord of house 2 and also the CSL of houses 4, 6, 10, 12 having no 
planet in its stars, and located in the sign of Aries of Mars. Star lord Ketu is an occupant 
of 10th house and conjoined with Mercury in 10, lord of 7,10 and Venus in 10, lord of 
6,11. 


So the 10% CSL Saturn signified houses 2, 6, 10 and is connected with Mars and Mercury, 
indicating promise of own press to the native, and I declared my opinion to the native. 


The native was happy and made a mouthful smile and began to talk. "Sir, I am not a 
wealthy man. I don't have a good capital to invest for a big industry. I have my own skill 
and experience of more than 15 years in the printing field but I have an old Duplo Ma- 
chine only. With that machine and my ability I wish to start my own printing business if 
you can recommend". With this innocent request, I casted his chart for his successfulness 
if he starts the business. 


If the native is going to start a new business, other two KP rules must be also satisfied in 
the natal chart for his success in the business. One is planetary chances for starting a 
new business and the next is to check the gain in business and the support of the Dasa, 
Bukthi and Anthar lords operating for both at the time of starting the business.

Prac cal Significators of Rahu/Ketu in KP 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 








BEE E EEE EEE EEE EEE EERE EEE Eee eee eee eee ee 


No Aspects of Rahu/Ketu 

The Moon's nodes, Rahu and Ketu, are not physical planetary bodies which can be seen 
through a telescope as we can see all the other planets. They are the imaginary points of 
intersection between the Sun's apparent orbital path around the earth, the ecliptic, and 
the Moon's orbital path around the earth. So logically these imaginary points of 
intersection, the nodes, cannot aspect any planet or house, and they are called shadowy 
planets. 





Maharshi Parasara did not mention the nodes’ aspects in hus classic Brihat Parasara Hora 
Sastra In the BPHS translated by R. Santhanam, Rajan Publications, page 255, chapter 


26: "Evaluation of Planetary Aspects", verses 2-5: “All planets aspect the 7 fully. Saturn, 
Jupiter and Mars have special aspects respectively on 3™ and 10%, 5tk and 9th , and 4% and 
8th “, Sage Varahamihira also did not exclusively touch Rahu/Ketu in his classic Brihat 
Jatalka. 


Classical Signification of Rahu/Ketu 
The classical signification of Rahu/Ketu as understood by K.S. Krishnamurti (KP Reader 
II, 1971 edition, page 315 ) is as follows: 


"Radu or Ketu will act as a strong agent to the planets to which they are conjoined. If they 
are not conjoined with any planet, then they give the results of the planet which aspects 
them. Only when they are neither conjoined with, nor aspected by any planet, they 
represent the lord of the house. (Uthrakalamrita -- Khanda VI Sloka 14 onwards)” 


Practical Signification of Rahu/Ketu in KP 
By taking into consideration of Rahu/Ketu's occupation and star lord, the following 
significators of Rahu/Ketu are practically applied in the KP Readers depending on 


relevance to the event under consideration regardless of their sequence of order (Rahu/ 
Ketu Rules in KP, in KPE-Zine, May 2007 issue): 


KP Ezine May 2015 147 


1) House occupied by Rahu/Ketu, 

2) Planet in conjunction with Rahu/Ketu, 
3) Planet in aspect to Rahu/Ketu, 

4) Star lord of Rahu/Ketu and 

5) Lord of sign occupied by Rahu/Ketu. 


Hindu conjunction in the same sign regardless of planetary positions from the beginning to 
end of sign and Hindu sign to sign aspects without taking consideration of orb are to be 
applied. 


The signification of planets in conjunction and in aspect, star lord and sign lord 
(significators 2-5) are generally to be considered by occupation and lordship of the relevant 
planet only i.e. not to go further up to the signification at star and sub levels. 


It is reasonable to consider the star lord of Rahu/Ketu only when Rahu/Ketu is a planet. 
Otherwise it will be consideration of the star lord of star lord in the case of Rahu/Ketu as 
star lord, and taking the star lord of sub lord in the cause of Rahu/Ketu as sub lord is the 
practice of 4-step method. 


Rahu/Ketu acts as agent of planets in conjunction and in aspect and its sign lord 
(significators 2,3 & 5). But it is not reasonable to say that Rahu/Ketu acts as agent of its 
star lord because it does not make sense to say that Rahu is agent of Rahu when Rahu is in 
the star of own or Rahu is agent of Ketu when Rahu is in the star of Ketu. 


In the computer printout of planet-wise grade A to D significators table, only Rahu/Ketu's 
occupation and its star lord's signification by occupation and lordship are included. So the 
signification of planets in conjunction or in aspect to Rahu/Ketu (significators 2 & 3) is also 
to be considered by occupation and lordship. 


Of course Rahu/Ketu can give the result of a house by occupation ‘very strongly’ only when 
there is no planet in the stars of Rahu/Ketu. In this case Rahu/Ketu also will become 
the strong significator of houses for which it is the cuspal sub lord. 

The following practice is not within the framework of the above practical significators - 1 to 
5: " Rahu/Ketu will offer the results of a planet which is deposited in the Rahu/Ketu star, 
eg. if Mars is deposited in the Rahu star, Rahu will offer the results of Mars by occupation 
and lordship." So it is not to apply this rule. 


One Way Signification of Rahu/Ketu 

In the case of planets in conjunction or in aspect (significators 2 & 3), Rahu/Ketu will give 
whatever the conjoined or aspecting planet is to give but the planet does not give whatever 
Rahu/Ketu is to give. This is one way signification of Rahu/Ketu as a result of not 
aspecting other planets as shadowy planet or imaginary point of intersection.

Father’s Death from Son’s Horoscope 


By: G.Subramanian 


13,Second Cross St., 
Chennai-35 


Email: gurusubra@yahoo.com 








\HERHEEEEE & 
It is an accepted principle in astrology that if the horoscope of an elderly person is not 
available, still it is possible to predict major events in his life from the available horoscopes 
of his son or daughter as the case may be. 

In recent years, many articles have appeared in astrological magazines to establish the 
validity of this concept. 

As an ardent enthusiast of astrology, I was also tempted to check this with regard to the 
death of a senior member of our family. 





The old gentleman passed away on the 5 of November 2002 around 6 A.M. I was able to 
locate his son’s horoscope from my records. I attempted to find out the occurrence of this 
sad event by suitably rotating the horoscope in such a way that the ninth house ( which 
represents the father) becomes the Ascendant of the departed soul. 


The original chart of the son is appended herewith for the study of our esteemed readers. 

At this juncture, it is worth recapitulating that houses 1, 3 and 8 are the primary houses 
for predicting the longevity of a person. We are also aware that the 12% to any house 
negates the results of the concerned house. Therefore, 12, 2 and 7, being 12‘ to the above 
houses are unfavorable houses for longevity known as Maraka houses. For Movable houses, 
11t house is termed ‘Badhaka’-, meaning death-inflicting house. 


Readers may note that houses 10, 3, and 8 of the original chart are houses 2, 7 and 12 of 
the rotated chart (treating the 9t as Ascendant). 

On a thorough examination of the rotated chart, it was clearly seen to belong to the 
category Of Poorna Ayush (Long Life) with longevity between 66 to 100 years. 

The significators of the Maraka and Badhaka (11) houses are as given hereunder in order of 
priority (planet in the star of occupant, occupant, planet in the star of owner, and house 
owner): 


House Planet in star of occupant Occupant Planet in star of owner Owner 
2 = — sun, Venus saturn 

7 — Rahu saturn Moon 
11 — — Kethu Mars 


The old gentleman breathed his last when his son was running Dasa, Bhukthi, Antara of 
Saturn-Kethu-Moon which are the prominent significators in the above tabulation. 


On the date of death, the luminaries and the period lords were transiting as follows: 

Sun in Rahu star Moon sub (Libra) 

Moon in Jupiter star Jupiter sub( Libra) 

Saturn in Mars star Venus sub (Gemini) 

Kethu in Saturn star Jupiter sub (Scorpio) 

I wondered how Jupiter finds a place in the above transits. After a little thought it occurred 
to me that Jupiter is a significator of the 12th house as a planet in the stars of owner, and 
house owner (128 house is for the end of life and Moksha). 

What an amazing system of prediction is K.P. system of astrology! We bow with deep 
reverence and gratitude to our revered and beloved Guruji Shri.K.S.K.

Background Note: Last year once I was in dire need of financial assistance. I did not know 
how to solve that financial problem or as to where and when would I get that financial

exclusively managed and disbursed upon on the self discretion of the boss. 

I made a K.P. horary chart upon the sanction of this emergency fund by the boss to help me 
with my emergency financial crisis. 

The question is whether a particular person (here it refers to my office boss) will help me 
financially or not? I at first casted the horary chart. The chart should be casted with divine 
number (horary or seed number between 1 to 249) depending upon my (astrologer’s) 
preference according to the knowledge, belief, experience and situation.

house represents cash & bank balance, jewelry and ornaments etc. and thus denotes

Question: Will misunderstanding between the two families make effect on marriage of their 
daughter and son that is to be materialized on 10 March 2015? 


Background: One of my known Mrs. X came to me and asked about a problem regarding a 
matrimonial matter related to her family. She told that the bridegroom family had got email 
from an unknown about affair of bride. Mrs. X belonged to bride family. Bridegroom family 
just shared this email with bride family. Bride family got into anxiety and mental agony too. 
Bride was not actually in any affair after deciding to marry with present one. Marriage date 
was already decided on 10 March 2015. So Mrs. X was worried whether this 
misunderstanding will cancel the decided marriage ceremony. She had great curiosity about 
KP astrology answer, so she asked question whether marriage will be solemnized or not. 
Question was related to an event which was to be happened or not happened in a few days. 


My View: I reframed the question. Firstly that whether both the families will be agreed or 
not on their decision to remain firm on decision of solemnized marriage on 10 March 2015. 
For that both the families need to talk on the issue and decide before 10 March 2015. I 
decided to do it with help of ruling planets because this was an event which will be 
answered by yes or no within a week from the date of question.

Rahu is agent of Mars.

days, only then it could be decided whether marriage will take place or not. I preferred to 
analyse it as event of yes or no that is supposed to be decided actually in 7 days. So I took 
day lord ‘Saturn’ as most important planet and deciding factor. 


Hints: Event which is to be occurred or not occurred, then on day of Asc sign lord planet 
from the day of day lord planet, the event will take place. Question was asked on Saturday 
which is the day of day lord Saturn.

2.3.15 it will be decided to cancel or not to cancel the marriage. I also cross checked Sun 
transit on these dates. Sun is in kumbh sign of planet Saturn. Presently Sun is going 
through satabhisha star of Rahu i.e. RP and that will remain there by 4 March 2015. Then

. References for manual adjustment are as follows: 


During World War II, from September 1, 1942 to October 14, 1945 (both days inclusive), 
all over pre-independence India, i.e. present day India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, clocks 
under Indian Standard Time were advanced by one hour, calling it as War Time. 
(“Astrology: How to Cast Your Own Horoscope”, by Dhamankar & Lagu, Madhusudan P. 
Lagu, Jaico Publishing House, 1984, pages 108 & 170) 

http: //www.wikiwand.com/en/Time in India 

From lst September 1942 to 14th October 1945, the Indian Standard Time was ad- 
vanced by one hour all over India including modern Bangladesh and Pakistan for pur- 
poses of daylight saving during the period and was thus 6h 30m ahead of G.M.T. Any 
recorded time of this period should therefore be reduced by 1 hour to get I.S.T. (Lahiri's 
"Indian Ephemeris", page 7, 2009 or any year under “Time reckoning in India”)

These areall based on objective evidence about the source of the data. 


Data as recorded by the family or state. This includes BC (birth certificate), and BR (birth record), that which 
Accurate is mot an official document but a quote of the birlh record trom the Regisirar or Bureau of Records, the 
laceurate baptismal certificate, family Bible, or baby book. These data reflect the best available accuracy. 


Taeger data groups: 1*,1F 


Data as quoted by the person, kin, friend, or associate. These data all come from someone's memary, family 
legend, or hearsay. The quote may be subsiantiated by a qualifying statement such as, "My grandfather 
wanted me to be born on his birthday and my mother said that | almost mace it. | was born three minutes 
belore midnight.” When the information comes from an astrologer's client, itis considered reliable, since a 
client is investing money for the astrologer's time and expertise. When ihe quote is Irom a public figure given 

A Accurate jp, public, it may be questionable. Please keep in mind that public figures, especially politicians, answer a 
question in public to be accommodating; therefore, the time given may not be accurate. When the quote is 
from one of a group of people who were asked casually, it might be questionable. Rounded-off time such as 6 
AM or midnight might also be questionable. 


Taeger data groups: 22° 2P aA 


Biography or autobiography. When these data are substantiated by a quote that qualifies the information, 
they are considered reliable, An example: “His grandmother arrived at 9 in the monning and barely had time 
to ramove her coat before mother gave birth.” Or, "Though she claims to have been born in 1946, state 
records clearly give September 5, 1942° or, “family legend reports ‘before noon'." When the quote is vague, 
B Blography Such as, "lt was a wild and stormy night,” a specific time may simply reflect the blagrapher's literary license. 
At times public figures lie about their age. Biographers who market scandal and gossip may actually create 
misiniormation for the sake of book sales. 
When data from books are specifically attributed to birth records, they are given a Rodden Rating of "AA".

Question -2: Rule for Deafness and Dumbness 
Please explain the astrological pattern for deafness and dumbness with an example chart. 


Answer -2: 

Hints for Disease 

In case of defective speech and sense of hearing (deafness and dumbness) the cuspal sub 
lord (CSL) of 6 ,8th , 12th houses signifies house 2 (speech), 3 (hearing), 6 (disease), 8 
(danger, serious ailment), 12 (defect) and is connected with Mercury (speech and hearing) 
and mute signs, (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces for dumbness) 

OR. The cuspal sub lord of 224 house (speech) and the 3rd house (hearing) is connected with 
the Maraka, Dadhaka, 6,8,12 houses. 

Hint for Cure from Disease: 

If the cuspal sub lord of 6 , 8 , 12th house signifies houses 1, 5, 11 (if not Badhaka), then 
native can be cured from disease during the joint dasa period (Dasa/Bhukti/Antra) of sig- 
nificators of house 1, 5, 11. 


Example Chart: Female, 24 September 1985, 19:45 PM IST, 22n18, 73e12, KPNA 23:34:03, 
Ascendant: Aries 02:53:32, Bal. Dasa: Moon 4Y, 10M, 12D 


Cuspal Analysis 

6th and 12th CSL Mercury+ is in house 6, owner of houses 3,4 and the CSL of houses 3, 4, 
6, 10, 12 having no planet in its stars. Mercury is in the star of Sun in house 6, owner of 
house 6, and sub of Venus in house 5, owner of houses 2, 7. Thus 6th and 12th CSL signifies 
houses 2, 3, 6,8,12 and is connected with Mercury for deafness and dumbness. 

It is also connected with Jupiter (manifesting the sound). 


8th CSL Saturn+ is in house 7, owner of houses 11, 12 and the CSL of houses 2, 8 having 
no planet in its stars. Saturn is the star of Jupiter in house 10, owner of houses 9, 10 and 
sub of Mars+ in house 5, owner of houses 1, 8. The 8 cusp and Saturn are placed in the 
mute sign Scorpio. So Thus 8th CSL signifies houses 2, 8,12 and is connected with the mute 
sign Scorpio for deafness and dumbness. Connection with Mars and Saturn also indicates 
seriousness and long term nature of disease. 


2nd CSL Saturn, as discussed above, signifies Maraka (2,7), Badhaka (11), 8, 12. 
3rd CSL Mercury, as discussed above, signifies Maraka (2,7), 6, 8, 12. 


Rules for deafness and dumbness are generally satisfied. 


Prospect for cure: 

6t and 12th CSL Mercury, as discussed above, signifies house 5 only for cure. 

8th CSL Saturn, as discussed above, signifies house 1, 5 for cure since house 11 is 
Badhaka. 

Jupiter Dasa will be running from 6 August 2015 to 6 August 2031. 

Dasa lord Jupiter is in house 10, owner of house 9,10, in the star of Mon in house 10, own- 
er of house 5 and sub of Rahu in 1, in sign Aries representing Mars+ in house 5, owner of 
1,8, signifying houses 1,5 for cure, along with very strong house 10 (12 to 11 - treatment 
not effective). 


Chance for cure is indicated but treatment may not be so effective.

Book Review- Mundane Astrology 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 





(‘EH 
Mundane Astrology 

by: Manik Chand Jain 

Sagar Publications, 1978, reprint 1992,..., 2007, pages 176 





This book “Mundane Astrology” by Manik Chand Jain is a free gift received along with 
Dr. Ravi Rao’s “A Nation’s Prophecy, Inclusive Methodology of Mundane Astrology” and other 
books which were ordered from Sapta Rishi Astrology online book store. 

http: //shop.saptarishisastrology.com/index.ph 


prod=76&cat=63&page=details&sub=More+Information 





This is the second book which has been strangely found to be a word-for-word copy of a 
Western astrological book. The first book is “Dictionary of Significators in Astrology” by 
Umang Taneja & P K Sarna, 2000, 235 pages, which is a word-for-word copy of Part One, 
An Alphabetical Listing, pages 3-163 of “The Rulership Book, A Dictionary of Astrological 
Correspondences”, by Rex E. Bills, American Federation of Astrologers, Inc., 1971, reprint 
2007, 440 pages. (Book Review, KP-Ezine January 2010 issue) In this Taneja’s book there 
is not much significant addition to Bills’ original. 


The core of Jain’s “Mundane Astrology” is also a word-for-word copy of Raphael's Mundane 
Astrology, first published in 1910. Raphael's original covers the fundamentals and a com- 
prehensive guide to the classic rules of Western mundane astrology. Raphael organizes his 
book house by houses telling how mundane houses work when planets are in them. In ad- 
dition, he also deals with solar and lunar eclipses and earthquakes. 


Raphael's Mundane Astrology is a part of the combined volume of three classical books on 
“Mundane Astrology, the Astrology of Nations and States” by H.S. Green, Raphael and C.E.O. 
Carter, Astrological Center of America, 2004, 308 pages overall. (Book Review, KP-Ezine No- 
vember 2012 issue) 


KP Ezine May 2015 179 


The entire text of Jane’s Mundane Astrology has been carefully reformatted from Raphael's 
original. Here are some additions like Pluto to Raphael's original saying in page 12 that 
Pluto is not a nice-seeming planet, but apparently we need his influence to 'round out' our 
lives - natal writing; a brief note on Rahu and Ketu, in page 13, which stand for plots, sedi- 
tions, lectures, underworld activities etc.; nature of zodiacal signs (Capricorn- Places signi- 
fied: barren, brushy, thorny places, fallow ground, etc. in page 26); rulership, exaltation, 
detriment and fall, as well as keywords of planets (for Sun- Keywords: power, vitality, self- 
expression and natal descriptions: superior or proud and haughty persons .. "Good": deal 
with superiors etc.) in pages 4-5; some data and examples in IST in pages 51-58, 60-61, 
112, 156-159 etc. But natal writing is not relevant for mundane astrology and Raphael’s 
original has not been significantly changed by including above facts and figures.

Finding lost answer sheets in a school 


By: Gunti Nagaraju KP astrologer 


M.com CAIIB, Retired Bank officer 
12-13-668/5/2, Second floor, Nagarjuna Nagar, 
Tarnaka,Secunderabad- 500 017; 

Tel: 040-27 172206; 949075237 1 

re ee Email: gunti.nagaraju@gmail.com 
‘HRERREEREEREERERERHEREERHEREEERHEEEEEEEEEEEEEHEHEEHEEEEEE & 
Will my lost answer sheets be found? If so, when? 

On 9 Feb 2012, Thursday, at 15 hours-25 minutes, I received a phone call from a known 
teacher requesting for a solution for her problem. She posed a question stating that she has 
lost corrected answer sheets of her class students somewhere in the school and she is 
unable to find them. She also said that she has to hand over the same on the same day to 
the headmaster before she leaves the school. She sounded panic and worried. When I asked 
her to give a number within 1 to 249, she without any hesitation spelled out number 5. 
Immediately I worked out the chart for the given number at 15H.27m.19sec. @ Secundera- 
bad 











1) As per the Gulbarga Theory “If the sub lord of the horary number furnished by the 
querent is also either the star lord of the ascendant or of the Moon star lord among the 
ruling planets, the result is YES”. 

As per the horary chart the sub lord of the horary number furnished is Mars. The star lord 
of the ascendant in the ruling planets is Rahu, and Rahu represents Mars. (Rahu is 
aspected by Mars and it is also posited in Mars sign Scorpio). 

So the answer for the query is YES, that is to say the answer sheets will be found. 


2) As per K.P. rules in horary- if the 11 cusp sub lord signifies 11t* and relevant houses 
under consideration the fructification of the event is promised. 

As per the chart 11 cusp sub lord is Rahu which signifies 11th at both levels and thereby 
it confirms that there is a promise of the event under consideration. 


3) As per K.P. rules, for predicting the event that has to happen within 24 hours, we can fix 
it by using the ruling planets. 

A) Lagna point must contain the R.P. only. 

B) The lagna sign lord, star lord and sub lord should be chosen according to the “first come 
first served” basis depending upon the hierarchy in which they appear in the R.P. list at the 
time of judgment. 

C) A ruling planet is strong by virtue of its level of appearance and not by the number of 
times it has appeared. 

D) However when the R.P. repeats itself- lagna point should also contain the same 
repetition. 


R.Ps. mean in the descending order of power: 
Asc Sub lord— Asc Star lord— Asc. Sign lord 
Moon Sub lord— Moon Star lord— Moon Sign lord — Day lord. 


For pinpointing the events that are expected to take place within 24 hours, we need to see 
when a proper lagna sign, star and sub arrive that contain in it the Ruling Planets that we 
received at the time of judgment. In other words if one is expecting something to happen 
within next 24 hours, our focus should be to trace the Asc. that will comprise of the sign 
Lord, Star Lord and Sub Lord which were found in the list of R.Ps. at the time of judgment. 
As per the chart the Ruling Planets at the TOJ are: 

Lagna-Gemini—Merc-Rahu-Mars 

Rasi- Leo- Sun-Ven-Sun

Once a lady from Sri Lanka, a new subscriber of KPEZine and a student of KP, had sought 
my astrological reading in connection with the health condition of a baby girl by writing the 
question, "I want6" CSL Venus is in housel2, owner of house 6, in the star of Mars in house

to know whether this native has any disease and does she has to suffer from any disease 
during on going Sun dasa?” 


Birth details: 

Baby Romaya, Female, 24 Sept.2014, 10.40 am, Castle Hospital, Colombo, Western 
Province, Sri Lanka, 06.54N, 79.53E, Asc. Scorpio 15° 16' 58", Sun Vimsottari Maha Dasa 
Balnce 01 Y, O06 M, 07 D, KP New Ayanamsha 23° 58' 21" , calculated by KPAstro 4.1 


As the question is regarding the health matter of the native, I directly looked at the 
Ascendant sub lord and found Jupiter is ruling the sub division of Lagna having the 
lordship of 2 (Maraka) & 5 (Free from diseases), located in the 9th, Badhaka house for the 
natives born in Scorpio fixed sign, and Jupiter is in the star of Mercury lord of 8 (Danger to 
life) & 11 (Recovery from ill-health) in 11. Jupiter is in the sub of Venus+, the lord of 7 
(Maraka) & 12 (Moksha/Renunciation/Hospitalization/Terminal/Untreatable), in the sign 
Leo (Heart) and falls in 10th (Treatment not effective/Retirement from this World) house. 
With these detrimental connection and signification of the Lagna sub lord Jupiter for 9, 8, 
2, 7, 12 indicates that the native is not in a good health condition in the on going birth 
Maha Dasa of Sun, which is in own star Sun in 10, lord of 10 and in the sub of Ketu in sign 
Pisces representing Jupiter in 9 (Badhaka), lord of 2, 5. 


Before scrutinizing the 6th cusp for diseases, a thorough check of Asc. cusp sub lord 
Jupiter has been done to find any clue for the ill-health of the native. The house where 
Jupiter is at the time of birth is Cancer, the 4th house of the natural Zodiac that is the seat 
of the heart and in the natal chart it is 9th Badhaka house. The star lord of Jupiter is 
Mercury. Although Mercury is a significator for 11 as owner and depositor, it is also a 
disease maker ruling the chest, lungs, veins and gall bladder. The star where Jupiter

liver. The sub of Jupiter is Venus in the 10th Leo, which rules heart, gall bladder.Based on 
these findings I concluded that something is wrong with any organ/s of the chest of the 
native.

If the sub lord of the Ascendant be the significator (in the star of the occupant or owner) of

Welcome back to another edition of the Novice Nook. Let’s get right to it. In the last issue, I 
demonstrated a chart with a question about longevity. How long will the person represented 
in the chart live? 

For those of you that have some experience in KP, I filled in many of the fields but with 
numbers and planets that were intentionally incorrect. The exercise was for you to 
substitute the fields with the correct numbers and planets. After going over the chart, you 
would have thus realized how to fix it for yourself. True, it was a challenging test. 

For those of you that are totally new to KP, I filled in the fields with the corresponding 
planets and numbers in this edition along with the steps and small explanations. Take a 
look at the chart Ref #1216 and let’s begin. 

Notice the set of six fields labeled Longevity. You will notice on the far left in the first field 
the numbers 6, or 8 or 12. These houses of significance are representative of the second 
field regarding to the life span of a person. Thus, if the cuspal sublord would be the 
significator of these three houses 6 or 8 or 12, the life span of the person will be 
approximately 33 years of age. 

If you look at the next two fields you will find the listing of the houses of 1 or 5 or 9 or 11 
( in another article, we will also discuss the checking of the 3™ and the 8 house) If the 
cuspal significator represents one of these above houses, the life span of person would 
approximately be about 66+ years of age. 

In the last two fields, if the cuspal significator represents the 6 or 8 or 12th and 1 or 5 or 
9 or 11, the life span the individual will be about 66 years. 

Several things have been demonstrated without explanation. It would take an entire book to 
explain everything including the nature of planets. This is where your own research will 
uncover some of the things you don’t understand. For instance, if you are not sure what 
Moksha or Maraka means, then you will have homework. If you are not sure what the 
difference between conjoined and conjunct or even what an aspect is, then you have more 
homework to do. If I give you everything, you would never appreciate this science as much 
and have nothing to share with the rest of the readers. If you discover or see something, 
email me a tdestechpress@aspoonfulLorg . 

Now, below, see each field in descending order represents a step in determining how to 
understand the chart you are reading.

Questions & Answers

(Hint & 


Question- 1: Transit in KP 

Can you explain how to use transit for timing of event . Suppose for marriage we get 7 
significators. Dasha bhukti is also of any of these 7 significators. How to decide the time of 
fructification of this event. CR Bhatt jis book says that in transit DBAS planets and or sun , 
moon - will be in star or sub of these same dbas planets .( or these significators of events). If 
star level is not necessary and the event can happen if transit is in fruitful sub of significator 
or dbas, then we will get many transit sensitive points. How to decide the right time ? 
Thanking you . 





Sir, i have a question regarding transit. For pinpointing timing after successfully clinching 
DBAS significators, the transit of significators including Su & Mo be in the cusps of the natal 
or horary chart or rashi? Becauz, cusps wld be overlapping the rashis? 

For ex. For a transit in 2nd cusp, as 2nd 3rd rashi may be having 2nd cusp, so can transit go 
up to 3rd rashi also, if star and sub corroborate the event? 

Appreciate your answer on my query. 


Answer - 1: 
In KP the cuspal sub lord indicates whether a matter is promised or not. The significators 
point out the time of event. Both dasa and transit must agree. 


Here are selection methods of fruitful significators: 

1) Significators of planets with no planets in their stars, which are the strongest 
significators of houses under consideration by sub lordship to them (Same as in Golden 
Rule: to take the planets which are posited in the sub of significators whose 
constellations are not tenanted.); 

2) Significators whose sub lords are the significators of houses under consideration; 

3) Significators which are the cuspal sub lords of houses under consideration; 

4) Significators appearing many times amongst significators. 


The DBA can be fixed by two ways. The first one is to check whether marriage is favorable 
starting from the current running Mercury Dasa (for marraigable age). If it is favorable, to 
check the current running Bhukti Jupiter and if the Bhukti is also favorable to choose the 
most favorable Antara Moon, and so on. If the current Dasa or Bhukti is not favorable, to 
move to the next or other favorable one. This is also the way done by KP astrologers without 
using the RPs, and the same way is applied in the four step method. This is also a KP usual 
way, not advancement to KP as some are saying. 


After fixing the DBA or DBAS, it is to check whether the chosen DBAS agree with the transit 
by the KP way. 


Generally an event happens during the joint DBAS period of the significators when transit 
agrees. Particularly at the time of event happening Sun, Moon and joint period DBAS lords 
are generally found to be transiting mainly in the star or sub of the same joint period DBAS 
lords or the significators of the event by the natal chart. 

Note: The significators of the star and sub in which the DBAS lords are transiting should 
be according to the bhava-based natal birth chart. 


KP Ezine June 2015 28 


In the KPAstro 4.1 SW developer Rangarajan Krishnamoorthy's computer analysis of 1005 
(one thousand & five) TOB AA rated marriage charts collected by Kanak Bosmia, transit 
DBAS lords, Sun, Moon are found transiting in the star & sub of DBAS lords by 79% (Dasa 
lord), 76% (Bhukti lord), 76% (Antara lord), 76% (Sookshma lord), 79% (Sun), and 80% 
(Moon) respectively on the date of marriage, in line with KP transit. 


For accurate timing, it is to choose the transiting Sun and Moon, which are mostly found 
in the star or sub of Sookshma lord at the time of event. For slow moving planets, in 
addition to stars and subs, the bhavas they are transiting may be also taken into account 
and needless to say the subs will decide the signification of transiting planets. 


In using the sensitive points, for the chosen DBA of fruitful significators for an event to 
materialize, say conjoined period of Sun, Venus, Mercury, then Sun sign, Venus star, 
Mercury sub; Venus sign, Sun star, Mercury sub, and Mercury sign, Sun star, Venus sub 
are the three sensitive and fruitful positions, which will be transited by Ascendant, 
Luminaries and the planets ruling the Dasa, Bhukti and Anthara. The sensitive positions 
when transited by the Ascendant degree, the exact hour and minute of the event can be 
told. If Moon is moved to that sensitive degree the day of the event can be arrived at. If the 
Sun, then month. If Jupiter, then the year can be arrived at. 


Fast or short predictions can be given just based on the Ruling Planets directly. A timing of 
an event can be fixed by using only the Ruling Planets calculated at a particular moment of 
time without resorting to the Natal or MHorary' chart as _§ follows: 


1) If an event is likely to take place within a few hours, move the Ascendant counting from 
the Ascending degree of the moment of judgment to the sensitive zone where one ruling 
planet becomes the sign lord, second ruling planet becomes the star lord and third 
ruling planet become the sub lord; 

2) If the event is expected to happen within some days, move the Moon to such a sensitive 
zone; or 

3) Ifit is to take place in some months, move the Sun; or 

4) If it is to happen in some years, Jupiter should be moved to find out the time of event.

fundamental rule: "The planet is the source, constellation indicates nature of the result 
and the sub is a deciding factor whether the matter is favorable or not." 


Planet Jupiter is in house 2, lord of houses 8-9-12; 
Jupiter is in the star of Mars in house 3, lord of house 7; 
Jupiter is in the sub of Moon in house 1, lord of house 4. 


House 2 is signified at grade B level, and so Jupiter is a significator for job.

and so Jupiter becomes the significator of houses 5,11. 


KP is 3-step only, i.e. planet, star and sub levels, and doesn’t consider 4-step. i.e. star of 
the sub. 

Considering the star of sub, in this case sub Moon’s star Sun, is K.M. Subramaniam’s 
Sublord Speaks and now it is called 4-step method which is KP based but not KP because 
rules are different and the result may not be the same.

Question - 5: A planet with no planet in its stars and a planet in its own stars 
Planet having no planet in its stars and planet in own star: If [A ] a planet is not a star lord to 
any one in a horoscope, [B] same planet alone in its own star, then what is the difference? 


Please pass on the complete reference of where KSK or CR Bhatt has used specifically the 

following parameters: 

a) The sub lord of a cusp is a strong significator of that cusp, if there is no planet in the stars 
of that sub lord (planet). 

b) If the planet is not the cuspal sub lord of any house, it will have only positional status, Le. 
it will be the strong significator of the house occupied by that planet. 

c) c) A planet in its own stars, having no planet in its stars, can have positional status but 
cannot be the strong significator of the houses under its sub lordship 

d) A planet in its own stars also having any other planet(s) in its stars can have neither 
positional status nor the role of strong significator of the houses under its sub lordship 


Answer -— 5: 

A planet having no planet in its stars becomes the strong significator of houses for which it 
is the cuspal sub lord. For example, no planet is in the stars of Sun, and this Sun is the 
CSL of 2,5,7 houses, then Sun becomes the strong significator of these houses. This is 
already time tested rule practically applied by many KP astrologers. 


This rule is related to the Golden Rule in KP, i.e. Take the planets which are posited in the 


KP Ezine June 2015 31 


sub of the significators whose constellations are not tenanted. (Astrosecrets & KP, Part II, p 
195) 

A planet in its star cannot be the strong significator of houses for which it is the cuspal sub 
lord because it has give its own result. 


Regarding the rule of no planet in the stars of a planet or golden rule, there is no direct 
spoon feeding references in the KP Readers other than the followings: 


“Besides this Mercury is also the sub-lord of Asc.,2"™d , 5th , 6th , 7th , Sth -J 1th and 12th 
cusp.” (KP Reader III, page 309/ 1971 edition, practical part, page 145). 


“3rd, 7th and 9th cusps fall in the sub of Saturn. . . Hence take Saturn too as a very 
strong significator”. (for foreign going) (KP Reader III, 1971 edition, practical part p 
151) But it is rewritten in “KP Reader III, p 316” like this:“Please note that Saturn is 
the sublord of 3rd and 9th cusp and no planet is tenanted in his star except himself.

Question - 6: Dasa and Transit 

Rule: Dasa Start and Condition of Dasa lord 

If a Planet at the time of commencement of its Dasa, attains its Natal Position (Sign wise), in 
transit then its Dasa will prove auspicious. 

The rule maybe checked, if its working! 


Answer -— 6: 
A matter promised in the natal chart will happen during the joint dasa period which 
signifies the required houses for that matter when transit agrees with the joint dasa (two to 
four levels). 


Dasa cannot give what is not promised in the natal chart. Transit cannot give what is not 
shown in the dasa. Horary cannot give what is not promised in the natal chart. 


Of course it's not easy to see this perfect harmony among natal chart, dasa and transit.

PREFACE 

“I shall not waste my days in trying to prolong them. i shall use my time”. These simple 
words were suggested in one or now popular .lames Bond novels, “You Live only once” , 
a fitting epitaph for him. If. therefore, any one fee’s the to know his days and the ways to 
use them, he can consult profitably.; not only his Doctor but his Astrologer as well. There 
are many who do not believe in the bad effects of ‘Rahukalam’ but all the same do not dare 
to disregard it. So is the attitude of thousands to Astrology. They scoff at it. belittle it, call it 
quackery and superstition. They have not the patience or the fairness to give it n study and 
a trial before rejecting it so outright. There are still others who cannot resist the temptation 
to have a try at it in private due to domestic compulsion, physical or mental suffering or 
friendly advice. 

It is not difficult for those who have belief in our Religion ant Veda to accept that 
“Jyotisham” is a Sastra occupying an honoured place in our System as a “Vedanga”, a limb 
or Anga of the Vedapurusha. An astronomer is a “Jyotisha” and “Jyotis" is light and 
“Jyotisha” is “light of the moon or stars” or for that matter, light on the dark or out-of-sight 
aspects of the past, present and the future. Thus implicit in this is, that planetary’ 
movements and positions at a given moment indicate, to a competent interpreter, the 
nature of the difficulties, current and to come, and the possible solutions relative to a 
particular time, period or aspect. 


It has been rightly said that Astrology is a Science of tendencies, and a fatalistic or 
deterministic approach to horoscopes and events is not called for. Astrology lays no claim 
to infallibility but, within limits, it can compare favourably with any other science. Let us 
not lose what it can offer for human progress and alleviation of suffering by set notions or 
prejudices. Let us not also make the unpardonable mistake of transferring the admitted 
deficiencies or the fallibility of the practitioner to the science itself. In this respect, it is no 
worse or no better than other subjects which we readily accept as Sciences. 


KP Ezine June 2015 34 


Jyotishmarthand Krishnamurti, the talented author of this work, is a tried and ex- 
perienced worker and researcher in the line He has the credit of discussing frankly and 
fully with all persons believers and non-believers, laymen and scholars, and making out a 
convincing case for a scientific and sustained study, with faith and belief, of this ancient 
knowledge. Several of his predictions have proved true and he has established a claim to 
reliability. 


A study of the present book will reveal the depth of his know-ledge and experience and his 
capacity to deal with the doubts and difficulties which a practitioner, new or old, is likely to 
come across and what is more, how the student should set about to resolve them. He has 
thus done a distinct, service -to the cause of Jyotisham and to its proper study and prac- 
tice. Iam sure that both lovers of Astrology and practitioners thereof, will be greatly profit- 
ed by this publication which in a sense may be called the teachers’ teacher. 


The author has devised a patent method of his own - called after him. Krishnamurti 
Padhdhati - which is claimed to have attained almost the infallibility of a formula. So be 
it. 


Of late, we are finding Astrology coming into its own ns a subject of interest to and study 
by eminent Scholars, Doctors of Philosophy, Literature, Medicine and Science, As- 
tronomers and others, deeply immersed in research and modern scientific knowledge. It 
has also been prescribed a subject of study on a par with other sciences in Universities. 
Colleges of Astrology awarding of diplomas and degrees have come into vogue. One need 
not accept or for that matter reject ancient or traditional knowledge and books merely _ be- 
cause they are so. Systematic, unprejudiced and scientific studies on modern lines are all 
to the good and are greatly to be welcomed. Books like the present one and astrologers like 
our author are sure to fill an honoured place in such efforts. 


I have great pleasure therefore in commending the author and his work. He has laboured 
long and true and deserves well of us. 


Mards-4 T. V. VISWANATHA AIYAR

The destiny and fruitfulness of an event 
- Cuspal strength 


By: Dr.G.K.Adith Kasinath 
Scientific KP Astrologer 
(lhce:101, Mullai Nagar, Near Shridi SaiBaba Temple, 
Suramangalam, Salem-5 Tamil Nadu. 
Website: www.bestkpastro.com 
: Cell: 09343419466 / 08015100700 
\RRERHREHEHEHEHEEHEEHEEEEEEHEREEEEEEEEEEEEEHEHEHEEEHEEE SE & 


I herewith like to furnish my views on the study on a cusp to know its destiny level. 











Normally the KP followers are just focusing on the cuspal Sublord of a particular cusp to 
know the destiny ie., whether the event will be fruitful or not. 


AS we are aware, as per KP if the Sublord is strongly connected to the favorable significa- 
tions, the event is promised. But in my view it does not mean that the event needs to be 
fruitful completely without considering the significations of Sign and Starlord.. 

Only when all these three rulers (sign, star and Sublord) are favorable the event is fruitful. 
If not, even though the event could happen due to the favorable Sublord, the fruitfulness 
would vary according to the sign and star lord’s significations. This decides the destiny lev- 
el. 


And the role of the Dasa Bukthi would further take the influence on the matter but within 
the limit fixed by the cuspal rulers. 


Now I like to explain this concept with an Example as given below: 


I COMPARE A CUSP WITH A CART WITH SOME STUFF ON IT WHICH IS MANUALLY 
DRIVEN BY A MAN. 


Let’s assume as follows: 
e “The CART” = “The SIGN LORD” 
e “The WHEELS of the Cart which are important = “The STAR LORD” 


e “The MAN who pulls the Cart to deliver the stuff who is most important = “The 
SUBLORD” 


e “The Road” that the Man comes across while taking the cart = “DASA / Bukthi/ 
Anthra and so on". 


Now the Man (SUBLORD) has to take the Stuff to the Destination by pulling the cart 
(Signlord) with the help of the wheels (Starlord) on the Road (Dasa Bukthi) 


On next page ==> 


KP Ezine July 2015 6 


DESTINY CUSPAL STRENGTH 
7 , 





| TRANSIMING 
PLANET 





SUBLORD SIGN LORD 





SOURCE 


DASA / BURKTHI 


STAR LORD 


For instance if the Man is strong enough, he can pull the cart and deliver the stuff to the 
destination. But the ultimate benefits of the stuff can be lesser if the cart, wheels and the 
road are weak. 


Similarly, even if the Cart, the Wheels and the roads are favorable, if the Man is completely 
weaker (drunk and unconscious or severely sick etc.,), he can not pull the cart at all. 


Hence the Destiny can experience different results according to the strength of the 
cuspal rulers. 


I have listed below the major possible combinations and the expected results one can 
experience: (the given examples are just for understanding purpose only) 


1) 

Sublord = Man : Strong 
Starlord =Wheel: Strong 
Signlord = Cart Strong 
Dasa/Bukthi = Road Strong 


Result : The Man can easily take the cart to the destiny on the road and deliver the source/ 
stuff satisfactorily. The event will be fruitful. 

2) 

Sublord = Man : Strong 

Starlord =Wheel: Strong 

Signlord =Cart Weak 

Dasa/Bukthi = Road Strong 


Result : The Man can take the cart to the destiny on the good road and deliver source. The 
quantity or level of benefits could be lesser as Cart is not strong enough to carry more 
weight 


3) 


Sublord = Man : Strong 
Starlord =Wheel: Strong 


KP Ezine July 2015 7 


Signlord =Cart Weak 
Dasa/Bukthi = Road Weak 


Result: The Man has to take more effort to take the weak cart on the weak road and deliver 
the source . The benefit level will be less with more wastage. But he will deliver some thing. 


4) 

Sublord = Man : Strong 
Starlord =Wheel: Weak 
Signlord =Cart Strong 
Dasa/Bukthi = Road Strong 


Result : 
The man has to put more effort to pull the cart as the wheels are weak. He would deliver 
with great obstacles. There will be some wastage also. 


5) 

Sublord = Man : Strong 
Starlord =Wheel: Weak 
Signlord =Cart Strong 
Dasa/Bukthi = Road Weak 


Result : 
If the wheels are completely damaged, the man can not easily pull. He may fail to pull the 
cart if the Road is also weak. Even a strong man can not help it. 


6) 

Sublord = Man : Strong 
Starlord =Wheel: Weak 
Signlord =Cart Weak 
Dasa/Bukthi = Road Strong 


Result : When Cart and also wheels are weak, the Man can take the cart with hard effort 
and losses with the support of the good road and deliver, But as the cart and wheels are

Biliary Atresia - KP Reveals 


By: Sumanadasa Namarathna | 


(Sunaparantha Kalyan) 
Ex-Accountant, Justice of Peace 
No.22/1, Udugampola Road, 
Marapola, Veyangoda, 
SRI LANKA 


Email: sunaparantha@gmail.com 











In my article "Infant Mortality" appeared in the KPEZine, June 2015 issue, I had discussed 
about a chart of an infant who died by the disease Biliary Atresia. The lady student of KP, 
also KPEZine reader, who gave me the chance to analyze the chart of the above baby, has 
sent me some more charts of the victims of above disease to analyze and find a KP rule for 
the same. 


Before I commence the analysis, I wish to give a brief introduction about Biliary Atresia to 
readers. The BILE also known as GALL, a product of liver is an essential fluid for digestion 
of foods intake. Bile makes cholesterol, fats, fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E & K and also de- 
stroys excess cholesterol and bilirubin. The reservoir of the bile made by the liver is called 
Gallbladder a small sack beneath the liver. When intake foods enter into the small intestine, 
a hormone called cholecystokinin secreted by the cells in the duodenum is released signal- 
ing the Gallbladder to pass the bile or gall to small intestine through the bile duct. If there 
is any obstruction in this biliary system or passing gall to the small intestine is called 
"Biliary Atresia". This disorder represents the most common surgically treatable cause of 
cholestasis (a condition where bile cannot flow from the liver to the duodenum) encountered 
during the newborn period. But this is a life threatening condition for infants in which the 
bile ducts inside or outside the liver don't have normal opening. 


With Biliary Atresia, bile becomes trapped, builds up, and damages the liver. The damage 
leads to scarring, loss of liver tissue, and cirrhosis. Cirrhosis is a chronic, or long lasting liv- 
er condition caused by scar tissue and cell damage that makes it hard for the liver to re- 
move toxins from the blood. These toxins build up in the blood and the liver slowly deterio- 
rates and malfunctions. The ultimate result of this dreaded disease is at the Karma of the 
native. Now let's discuss astrologically about three died babies and one alive baby suffering 
from this disease.

Hints 

If the cuspal sub lord of the 4th (Land/Building) be the significator of 4 (Land/Building), 11 
(Success/Fulfillment of desire) or 12 (Investment), one will have his own building during the 
joint period of the significator of 4, 11 and 12. 


Cuspal Sub Lord: 

4th Cusp (Pisces 06°.34’.33”): 4 cusp sub lord is Mercury. Mercury is occupant of 5, 
owner of 8-10. Star lord Ketu is occupant of 6. Ketu is conjoined with Venus. Venus is 
occupant of 6, owner of 6-7-11. No planet is in the star of Venus and Venus is the CSL of 
3-9. Mercury is in the sub of own. Thus 4th cusp sub lord signifies 6-7-11-3-9 and 
connected with 5-8-10. Thus 4 sub lord Mercury indicates 11. 


He have asked for "Villa" which means luxurious type, thus it needs to check 11 cusp sub 
lord also. 


11th Cusp (Libra 07°.27’.16”): 11 cusp sub lord is Rahu. Rahu is in the star and sub of 
Mercury. Rahu is occupant of 12. No planet is in the star of Rahu and Rahu is the CSL of 
2-5-11. Rahu is conjoined with Saturn. Saturn is occupant of 12, owner of 3. Star and sub 
lord Mercury is owner of 5 and occupant of 8-10. Thus 11 CSL Rahu is signifies 5-8-10 
and connected with 12-2-5-11-3. Thus indication is 11 also here. 


Joint period: 
At the time of judgment, you are running Mercury Dasa from 06-05-2011 to 06-05-2028. 
You are running the joint period of Mercury-Venus up to 31-07-2017. 


Dasa lord Mercury is in the star of Ketu and sub of own. Mercury is occupant of 5, owner of 
8-10. Star lord Ketu is occupant of 6. Ketu is conjoined with Venus. Venus is occupant of 6, 
owner of 6-7-11. No planet is in the star of Venus and Venus is the CSL of 3-9. Dasa lord 
signifies 6-7-11-3-9 and is connected with 5-8-10. Thus this dasa lord indicates buying a 
Villa. 


Bhukti lord Venus is in the star of Moon and sub of Mercury. Venus is occupant of 6, owner 
of 6-7-11. No planet is in the star of Venus and Venus is the CSL of 3-9. Star lord Moon is 
occupant of 7. Sub lord Mercury is occupant of 5, owner of 8-10. Thus bhukti lord Venus 
signifies 7 and is connected with 6-7-11-3-9-5-8-10. So this bhukti indicates buying a Villa. 


My opinion: You will buy a "Villa" by next year for sure. 


Outcome: Prediction comes correct.

promised during the joint period of the significators of 2, 6 and 10.

Question - 1: Birth Time Rectification 

Sir, Iam a beginner in KP field and I am very confused about BTR process in KP as KP is 
purely based on sub lord and the sub lord is very sensitive changing in approx 3 min, so it is 
very difficult to calculate without point error birth time, normally people don't have this accu- 
rate recorded time. 


Secondly BTR process is purely based on ruling planets and on accessing it by different as- 
trologers. We always get different RPs so it is quite difficult to get accurate sub lord of as- 
cendant. 


Moreover I personally concern with two different KP astrologers and both give me different 
readings. 

First one gives 15:08, Asc in Cancer-Saturn-Ketu 

Other one 

14:45, Cancer-Jupiter-Rahu sub 


Answer- 1: 

KP is the sub lord theory and accurate birth time is required as Lagna moves 1 degree per 
4 minutes, and as the shortest time, Sun sub can change by (800 X 6)/120 = 40 minutes, 
i.e. by time of 2 minutes 36 seconds. 


However astrology is divine science, and so recorded birth times are used in the solved ex- 
amples of the KP Readers without any prior birth time rectification (BTR). 


Finding accurate birth time may be like a wild goose chase only, and anybody can apply 
any rule that works for him since even the moment of birth is not known for sure whether 
it is the time of taking the first breath or the time of the head emerging from the mother’s 
body or the time of the first cry or the time the whole body emerging out of the mother’s 
body or the time of cutting the umbilical chord. 

https://groups.yahoo.com/neo/groups/k p_ system/conversations/messages/34875 


Under these conditions, if and only if the birth time is doubtful by the consultant, the 
birth time rectification (BTR) is to be done by the help of well tested ruling planets (RPs)- 
based BTR method with verification. 

https: //groups.yahoo.com/neo/groups/k _ p system/conversations/messages/30596 


Otherwise the astrologer might be responsible for mental damage caused by the controver- 
sial prediction as a result of unnecessary and unreliable BTR by adding some more drops 
in the ocean of uncertainties. 


Because RPs cannot help an astrologer all the time, and depending on astrologers, meth- 
ods, time and space, the RPs and consequently rectified birth time can be different for the 
same native, as in the case of Indira Gandhi's birth time, and so the rectified birth time is 
given grade C only after grade AA, A and B.

“Note the sub lord of the sixth (6th) cusp. This needs correct moment of birth. If it is not

Question- 2: Dr. Kar’s Theory of Short Prediction (TSP) 

In TSP by Dr. Kar, what to be taken (location) 82.30 + our location (say I’m from Hyderabad 
which comes to 17.46 degrees approx) or only Hyderabad planets at 5.30. Which location to 
consider? Request you to throw some light on this. 


Whether the effects of Saturn has to be considered always? Please guide. 
Answer- 2: 


In casting the TSP chart (1-249) or (1-2193), to take the Time always at °5:30AM IST’ of the 
day of judging the query, irrespective of whatever time of judging on that day, ie. 00:00 
GMT for casting the chart outside India. 


For location, place of judgment is to be taken, in this case Hyderabad . 


Regarding Saturn’s effect, it depends on one's practice or belief like retrogression whether 
to consider or not. In some Kanak Bosmia's failed 2008 cricket world cup predictions, not 
consideration of Saturn's effect is found to be a reason of failure. 


Question- 3: Casting a Horary Chart 

I would be grateful if someone would clarify about this. In the present time of fast and easy 
communication it is not uncommon for the questioner (consultant) and the person who does 
the analysis to be in different locations, often in different zones. The questioner gives a num- 
ber between 1 and 249. When the horary chart is drawn by the analyzer (living in different 
time zone) should he use his own local time and location or should he use the time and loca- 
t ion o f t h e q ueostiooneor ? 


Also, should the time at which the questioner gives the number or the time at which the ana- 
lyzer begins the analysis is used for drawing the chart? 


KP Ezine July 2015 37 


Answer- 3: In a horary chart, time of judgment is the time at which the astrologer or ana- 
lyzer casts the chart to begin the analysis, not the time at which the questioner gives the 
horary number. 


In casting a horary chart, the astrologer or analyzer should use his own local time and lo- 
cation, not the time and location of the questioner. 


Question- 4: 

I am learning KP astrology, I have some doubts about conjunction & aspects, so please clari- 
Ju. 

Suppose the 4th bhava is in Tula at 269 & the 10th bhava is in Mesha at 26° - 

Guru at Tula 229, Rahu at Tula 149° & Kuja at Tula 06° 

Sukra at Mesha 18°, Ketu at Mesha 14° Buda at Mesha 29° & Sun at Taurus 2° 

Please explain about conjunction & aspects among these entire planets. 


Answer- 4: Aspects and Conjunction in KP 

In KP, as applied in the solved examples of the KP Readers, Hindu conjunction in the same 
sign regardless of planetary positions from the beginning to end of sign and Hindu sign to 
sign aspects without taking consideration of orb are applied. 


Guru at Tula 22°, Rahu at Tula 14°& Kuja at Tula O6° are considered to be conjoined as 
all these planets are in the same Tula sign. 


Sukra at Mesha 18°, Ketu at Mesha 14° Buda at Mesha 29°%are also considered to be con- 
joined as all these planets are in the same Mesha sign. 


Kuja aspects Sukra, Ketu and Budha by 7 aspect and Ravi by 8" aspect. 
Guru aspects Sukra, Ketu and Budha by 7‘ aspect. 

Sukra aspects Guru, Rahu and Kuja by 7 aspect. 

Budha aspects Guru, Rahu and Kuja by 7 aspect. 


Aspect of Rahu/Ketu is not applied in KP. The Moon's nodes, Rahu and Ketu, are not 
physical planetary bodies which can be seen through a telescope as we can see all the oth- 
er planets. They are the imaginary points of intersection between the Sun's apparent or- 
bital path around the earth, the ecliptic, and the Moon's orbital path around the earth. So 
logically these imaginary points of intersection, the nodes, cannot aspect any planet or 
house, and they are called shadowy planets. 


The Hindu zodiac is used to consider the Hindu conjunction and aspects, and the bhava 
chart with Placidus cusps are used to consider the bhava occupied by planets. 

If the 4th cusp is in Tula at 26° Guru at Tula 22°, Rahu at Tula 149°& Kuja at Tula 06° are 
the occupants of 34 house. 

If the 10th cusp is in Mesha at 26° Sukra at Mesha 18°, Ketu at Mesha 14° are the occu- 
pants of 9 house and Budha at Mesha 29° is the occupants of 10‘ house.

Medical Astrology 
by Dr. Shanker Adawal

This book ‘Medical Astrology’ is a collection of materials composed by various authors who 
have worked in this field and the author has tried to build it up gradually so that the com- 
piulation can be understood of this complex topic. All the 
slllbjects discussed in this book are based on the fundamen- 
Medical Astrology Lal «and basic cannons of the Indian and western Astrology. 


4 wide area of medical astrology is covered in this book, as 
shown in the contents. The indicators of planetary combina- 
ion for diseases have been provided in chapter 22: 
Astrology Significatiors of Health Problems’ (pp 153-201). 
Important diseases have been explained elaborately in chap- 
ler 43: ‘Case Studies of Disease Through Medical Astrology’ 
with support of many illustrations from actual life (pp 202- 
207), 


In his studies and research the author has found that as- 
trology can point to chronic health problems usually indi- 
3 cated by the Sun, Ascendant, 6th house and the signs asso- 
Boece ciated with them. If one has Venus in poor aspect and poor- 
es ly placed, as well as on the cups of the 6th house, well then, 
watch the sweets or one will end up a diabetic, especially if 
the Moon is added te the mix. Venus rules sweets and the kidneys. The Moon rules fluids, 
including to some extent the blood. If you have a Leo Ascendant with the Sun in the 6th, 
look out for heart and back problems. 





Neptune rules things that are hidden. The author finds Neptune/Pisces prevalent with 
cancer diagnoses or other hard to diagnose illnesses until which time they are found. Jupi- 
ter can also be a cancer indicator when there is a tumor involved due to its association 
with excess growth. Mars and Neptune, or Aries and Pisces are often times found in charts 
of violent suicide. The act (for instance, a gun to the head) is easy to see in hindsight with 
Mars being the violence and Neptune being something done in secret. Mars in the 1*t 
house is a dangerous placement for head wounds, but can also denote great athleticism 
and a courageous soul. 


Neptune is far more ominous and can include ailments pertaining to drug use, drowning, 
and with Gemini pneumonia. Cancer as a disease is often associated with Neptune be- 
cause it quietly and insidiously destroys cell tissues. If Neptune is prevalent in the chart, 
look at its sing placement and be cognizant of changes in the area of the body ruled by 
that sign. Early detection is often the greatest hope for people with cancer. Cancer, as a 
sign, and the Moon, when associated with Neptune are the rulers of communicable disease 
like tuberculosis, AIDS, Ebola and other scary transmutable.
